subject: Post-call: cost gating & pilot commitment checklist
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Owen Park <owen.park@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, May 4, 2026 at 9:12 AM -0700
Subject: Post-call: cost gating & pilot commitment checklist

Hi Owen — thanks again for a focused conversation this morning. Quick write-up of what we heard, our proposed pilot scope, and the asks to keep the budget gate clear so your finance team can sign off.

What we heard (pain / goal):
- Primary pain: token burn from high-cardinality prompts (NLP enrichment + receipts parsing) is driving variable monthly costs that are hard to forecast.
- Secondary: occasional 95th-percentile latency spikes affecting UX for some merchant flows.
- Business goal: validate a production-like pilot that keeps unit cost < $0.005/token equivalent for peak flows and stays within a $50k Q3 budget guardrail.

Key cost levers we recommended during the call:
1) Batching: micro-batching + concurrency shaping (expect ~25–40% per-token cost saving at QPS=15–30 for your traffic shape).
2) Prefix/KV caching: for repeated prompts (merchant profile + known fields) — should reduce repeat token generation by ~20–30% on targeted endpoints.
3) Model routing / variant selection: route low-criticality flows to a faster, quantized model variant to lower cost.
4) Quantization: 8-bit or mixed-precision candidate for non-sensitive paths to further reduce GPU footprint.

Proposed pilot scope (30 days nominal):
- Traffic: production-like replay of the attached acme-traffic-sample.csv (we discussed 10–25 TPS bursts).
- Targets: median latency < 220ms; p95 < 700ms; token-equivalent unit cost <= $0.005 for peak windows.
- Telemetry: full token-level billing + latency traces (we will share a dashboard link).
- Success criteria: demonstration of cost < $0.005 OR a deterministic, documented path to reach that with quantization/batching within 2 weeks.

Asks / next inputs from Acme (to unblock procurement/finance):
- Confirm the $50k Q3 budget guardrail is the right constraint and whether it needs to be split across months.
- Provide a short list of security/compliance owners we should loop in for SOC 2 evidence (we have a pack attached).
- Approve pilot start window (we suggested May 17) and access for a short production-like replay.

Attachments: pilot-scope-draft.pdf (attached), acme-traffic-sample.csv (you emailed this in the call), SOC2 evidence pack referenced as soc2-evidence-pack.zip

Next steps we propose:
- If you confirm budget/scope today, we’ll put together an SOW-lite and a simple mutual action plan (MAP) mapping milestones to signoffs (pilot start, mid-pilot check, final decision).
- Karthik will scope batching/cache params and send a cost-sensitivity table (tokens/latency vs config).
- Marissa can join procurement cadence to speed contract & PO.

Owen — does this capture everything accurately? Any immediate redlines to scope or budget?

Thanks,
Camila

Subject: Re: Post-call: cost gating & pilot commitment checklist

Thanks Camila — this is helpful and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Budget: yes, $50k is our Q3 allocation for this initiative. Ideally we’d like a one-month pilot that fits into a $25k monthly cap, but we can be flexible if the first month shows obvious cost reduction. Finance will need a firm ceiling.
- Security: please loop in our Head of Security (Leah Nguyen, leah.nguyen@acmepayments.com) and Procurement (Samir Patel, samir.patel@acmepayments.com). SOC 2 docs look fine — we’ll have legal request a short checklist.
- Traffic sample: attached the CSV you referenced (confirming it has our spike/batch windows). The numbers are representative: peaks around 25 TPS for checkout flows, sustained ~6 TPS for enrichment.

Can you include an explicit cost-sensitivity table that shows: current baseline cost (our current provider), expected cost with batching-only, expected cost with batching+cache, and expected cost with batching+cache+quantization? We want a simple 3-row table we can paste into an internal deck for Finance.

Also — procurement will want estimated time-to-production for a Dedicated pool vs Hosted API. Are there differences in price predictability you can highlight?

I’ll tentatively hold May 17 for a pilot kickoff if you can get the SOW-lite over by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Owen
Owen Park | Product Lead, Integrations | Acme Payments
own.park@acmepayments.com | +1 (650) 555-0119

Owen / Camila — rapid technical clarifications and a proposed cost-sensitivity outline: 

1) Batching: for Acme's burst profile (25 TPS peaks), configure a hybrid queue: max_batch_size=64, batching_timeout=12ms, concurrency_target=8. We expect 30–35% per-token savings for generation-dominant flows.
2) Cache: KV prefix cache on merchant-profile queries should hit ~22% of requests per the sample. That’s another ~20% reduction in generated tokens for those endpoints.
3) Quantization: recommending int8 for low-risk paths; we’ll validate quality on a 48-hour run. Int8 expected to reduce model cost by ~30–40% on GPU throughput cost.

Attached (inline table in my note):
- Baseline: $0.009/token (current vendor estimate you shared)
- Batching-only: $0.0062/token (approx)
- Batching + Cache: $0.0049/token
- Batching + Cache + Int8: $0.0034/token

Those are rough midpoints — I’ll produce a formatted table (CSV and one-slide PNG) for Finance that maps tokens-per-minute -> monthly spend at different QPS.

If we need price predictability for Procurement, Dedicated pools give predictable throughput pricing (monthly commit + per-node overage) whereas Hosted is pay-as-you-go and will show variance month-to-month unless you set strict quota policies. We should include a simple cost comparison in the SOW-lite.

I’ll push the sensitivity table by EOD.

—Karthik
